p: there were in the church that: Paul with Barnabas is again the second time appointed apostle of the Gentiles, not of man, neither by man, but by an extraordinary commandment of the Holy Spirit.
Herod the tetrarch: This was the same Antipas who put John the Baptist to death.
ministered to the Lord: While they were busy doing their office, that is, as Chrysostom expounds it, while they were preaching.

called them: The Lord is said to call, from which this word "called" comes from, which is common in the Church, when he causes that to be which was not, whether you refer it to the matter itself, or to any quality or thing about the matter: and the use of the word "call" has come about because when things begin to be, then they have some name: and furthermore this also declares God's mighty power, in that he spoke the word, and things were made.
And when they had fasted and: Fasting and solemn prayers were used before the laying on of hands.
So they: Paul and his companions first bring Cyprus to the subjection and obedience of Christ.
Seleucia: Seleucia was a city of Cilicia, so called after Seleucus, one of Alexander's successors.
But Elymas the sorcerer: The devil makes Christ's victory more glorious in that he sets himself against him.

And said: The sorcerer, who was stricken by Paul with a physical punishment (although extraordinarily), shows an example to lawful magistrates how they ought to punish those who wickedly and obstinately hinder the course of the Gospel.
mischief: He points out a fault of those who run eagerly and with great desire into all types of wickedness with the least bit of prompting from the world.
hand of the Lord is upon: His power which he shows in striking and beating down his enemies.
Now when Paul and his company: An example in one and the very same group of people both of singular steadfastness, and also of great weakness.
Pisidia: This distinguishes between it, and Antioch which was in Syria.

And after the reading of the: In the Synagogue of the Jews (according to the pattern of which Christian congregations were instituted) the Scriptures were read first, then those who were learned were licensed by the rulers of the Synagogue to speak and expound.

have any word of exhortation for: Literally, "If there is any word in you": this is a kind of speech taken from the Hebrews, by which is meant that the gifts of God's grace are in us, as it were in treasure houses, and that they are not ours, but God's. In the same way David says, "Thou hast put a new song in my mouth"; Ps 40:3.
Then Paul stood up: God bestowed many wonderful benefits upon his chosen Israel, but especially this, that he promised them the everlasting redeemer.
exalted the people when they dwelt: Advanced and brought to honour.
high arm brought he them out: Openly and with strong power, breaking in pieces the enemies of his people.

four hundred and fifty years: There were from the birth of Isaac until the destruction of the Canaanites under the governance of Joshua four hundred and forty-seven years, and therefore he adds in this place the word "about", for three years are missing; the apostle, however, uses the whole greater number.
forty years: In this space of forty years the time of Samuel must be counted and included with the days of Saul, for the kingdom did as it were include his administration.
Of this man's seed hath God: He proves by the witness of John that Jesus is the Saviour who would come from David.
before his coming the baptism of: John as a herald did not show Christ coming from afar off, as the other prophets did, but right at hand and having already begun his journey.
Men and brethren: Christ was promised and sent appropriately to the Jews.

For they that dwell at Jerusalem: All things came to pass to Christ, which the Prophets foretold concerning the Messiah: so that by this also it appears that he is the true and only saviour: and yet nonetheless they are not to be excused who did not only not receive him, but also persecuted him most cruelly, even though he was innocent.

But God raised him from the: We must set the glory of the resurrection against the shame of the cross, and the grave. And the resurrection is equally proved by the witnesses who saw it, and by the testimonies of the Prophets.
hath raised up Jesus again: For then he appeared plainly and manifestly as the only Son of God, when he left behind his weakness and came out of the grave, having conquered death.
as it is also written in: If Christ had remained dead, he would not have been the true Son of God, neither would the covenant which was made with David have been certain.

sure mercies of David: The Greeks call those things "holy things" which the Hebrews call "gracious bounties": and they are called David's bounties in the passive voice, because God bestowed them upon David. Moreover, they are termed "sure", after the manner of speech which the Hebrews use, who terms those things "sure" which are steady and certain, and such things which never alter or change.
Wherefore he saith also in another: The Lord was in the grace in such a way that he experienced no corruption.
Be it known unto you therefore: Christ was sent to give them free remission of sins who were condemned by the Law.
all things: Whereas the ceremonies of the Law could not absolve you from your sins, this man absolves you, if you lay hold of him by faith.
Beware therefore: The benefits of God turn to the utter undoing of those that condemn them.
And when the Jews were gone: The Gentiles go before the Jews into the kingdom of heaven.
religious proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas: Who had forsaken their heathen religion, and embraced the religion set forth by Moses.
But when the Jews saw the: The favour on the very same Gospel is to the reprobate and unbelievers death, and to the elect and those who believe it is life.
Then Paul and Barnabas waxed bold: The Gospel is proclaimed to the Gentiles by the express commandment of God.
judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life: By this your doing you pronounce as it were sentence upon yourselves, and judge yourselves.

ordained to eternal life believed: Therefore either all were not appointed to everlasting life, or either all believed, but because all did not believe, it follows that certain ones were ordained: and therefore God did not only foreknow, but also foreordained, that neither faith nor the effects of faith should be the cause of his ordaining, or appointment, but his ordaining the cause of faith.
But the Jews stirred up the: Such is the craft and subtlety of the enemies of the Gospel, that they abuse the simplicity of some who are not altogether evil men, in order to execute their cruelty.
devout and honourable women: Those who embraced the Law of Moses.
But they shook off the dust: The wickedness of the world cannot prevent God from gathering his Church together, and to foster and cherish it, when it is gathered together.
